reputation.summary: Not a hi-fi favourite. Its fame comes from guitar pedals: the JRC4558D in the Ibanez TS-808 Tube Screamer (1979) and BOSS SD-1, credited with warm, mid-forward overdrive. In hi-fi it is the cheap default in 1980s–90s budget gear; Soomal ranks it below the NE5532 and NJM4580. Jazzcaster found glossy and matte JRC4558D near-identical in tone, glossy quieter.
typical_uses: Tube Screamer, TS9 and SD-1 overdrive pedals
Budget cassette decks, mini-systems, sound-card outputs
General filters and buffers on ±15 V or 9 V
Synth, Eurorack and retro-console audio stages
caveats: Slow: 0.8–1.7 V/µs gives only about 13–27 kHz full-power bandwidth at 20 Vpp.
Phase reversal when the input comes within about 1 V of V− (CM range ±12 V min).
Rated only into 2 kΩ, so not a headphone driver; 25–150 nA bias adds offset with high-impedance sources.
Vendor dies differ (Raytheon, TI, JRC, NJM4558C), so 'a 4558' is not one sound or spec.
Vintage JRC NOS premiums attract fakes and relabels.

counterfeit_notes: Premium 'NOS vintage JRC4558D' listings, glossy (艶あり) ones included, are often fakes. 4558s are also remarked as JRC4580; a slew (~1 V/µs) or GBW (~3 MHz) check exposes them. Genuine TI markings: RC4558P, R4558, R4558I, YRP/YRS/YRU. Buy from authorized distributors.
alternatives: Pedals: TI RC4558P or NJM4558D stock

part_numbers_affected: RC4559P / RC4559DR (sibling part in the same PCNs)
silicon_changes.identification: Datasheet G → H. Datasheet PCN 20241230001.1 (2 Jan 2025, first ship 2 Apr 2025) cites PCN 20240723003. Lots after Oct 2024 likely new silicon; no marking rule.
silicon_changes.summary: TI moved RC4558 from SFAB 150 mm to RFAB 300 mm (PCN 20240723003, first ship 21 Oct 2024) and re-specified it in Rev H: 4 MHz, 6.5 nV/√Hz, 2.2 V/µs, 0.0001% THD+N, 10–30 V. Shifts this large imply a revised die. It does not match TI's shared NE5532-class die (inference).
silicon_changes.audio_impact: On paper quieter (~1.8 dB) and faster. Overdrive character, clipping and recovery may differ; 9 V pedals sit below the 10 V minimum.
silicon_changes.compatibility_risk: medium – same pinout; 33% more GBW may cut phase margin, and 9 V pedals are below spec.
silicon_changes.verification: Rev H headline specs and PCN 20241230001.1 citing PCN 20240723003 confirmed; that PCN's title not retrieved.

silicon_changes.vendor: Raytheon vs Texas Instruments vs JRC (independent second-source dies)
silicon_changes.identification: Logo and prefix: Raytheon RC4558N/M; TI RC4558P/DR marked 'RC4558P' or 'R4558'; JRC/NJR NJM4558D marked 'JRC4558D'.
silicon_changes.summary: One generic number, separate vendor designs. The Raytheon, TI and JRC datasheets differ materially in typical figures, and Raytheon's schematic differs from JRC's equivalent circuit, pointing to independent dies. TI's RC4558 was later revised again (see the 2024 entry).
silicon_changes.audio_impact: Small: all are 3 MHz 741-class parts. Pedal users report TI RC4558P vs JRC4558D tonal differences (folklore). All trail 5532 and 4580 in hi-fi.
silicon_changes.compatibility_risk: low – same pinout, supply range and compensation.
silicon_changes.verification: Based on the Raytheon, TI and JRC datasheets.

silicon_changes.identification: Datasheet version (Ver.2013-11-05 or later vs the old databook). No marking or suffix change.
silicon_changes.summary: JRC re-characterised the NJM4558 in Ver.2013-11-05: the operating range widened from −20/+75 °C to −40/+85 °C and typical bias is quoted as 25 nA instead of 50 nA. Ver.2019-02-21 (NJM4558 only) followed. No die change is documented.
silicon_changes.compatibility_risk: low – same part, wider rated temperature range.
silicon_changes.verification: Ver.2013-11-05 and the −40 to +85 °C range confirmed; the 25 nA figure not seen.

silicon_changes.vendor: JRC / NJR (glossy Japan-made vs matte overseas-made JRC4558D)
silicon_changes.when: 1980s glossy vs later matte; no PCN
silicon_changes.identification: Package finish (glossy vs matte), country of origin, JRC vs NJR logo, date/lot code. No PCN or suffix change.
silicon_changes.summary: Jazzcaster, a Japanese hobby site, says glossy JRC4558D/DD parts came from JRC's Saga (Kyushu) plant and matte ones from overseas; JRC never documented this. In its TS-circuit tests harmonics above 440 Hz were almost identical, differences appeared only below 80 Hz, and glossy parts were clearly quieter, especially at HF.

spec_deltas.parameter: Measured noise floor (Jazzcaster TS rig, not a datasheet spec)
spec_deltas.after: matte (overseas): higher, spread over a wider band

silicon_changes.audio_impact: Minor: same pedal tone, slightly lower noise for glossy. The author judged only 2–3 in 100 listeners could tell. Irrelevant for hi-fi.
silicon_changes.compatibility_risk: low – same part number, pinout and ratings.
silicon_changes.verification: Based on Jazzcaster's published tests and Japanese forum posts.

silicon_changes.identification: Distributor and Nisshinbo lifecycle status for the DIP-8 NJM4558D.
silicon_changes.summary: Distributors list the DIP-8 NJM4558D ('JRC4558D') as discontinued, with remaining stock only. The Nisshinbo NJM4558 series page and the NJM4558C remain. No official successor statement was found.
silicon_changes.audio_impact: None electrical. Treat new 'JRC4558D' DIPs offered now with suspicion (old stock or counterfeit).
silicon_changes.verification: Distributor listings show discontinued/EOL; no Nisshinbo notice number found.

silicon_changes.identification: Orderable number contains 'NJM4558C' (e.g. NJM4558CG-TE2). Top marking unconfirmed; check the full part number and datasheet.
silicon_changes.summary: Nisshinbo sells the NJM4558C as a separate product with different specs (1.5 vs 1 V/µs, 3.5 vs 3 MHz), suggesting a newer die. With the DIP NJM4558D gone it may become the main Nisshinbo 4558, but no official successor statement was found.
silicon_changes.audio_impact: Slightly faster. TS-pedal tone may differ from the classic JRC4558D; untested.
silicon_changes.compatibility_risk: low – same dual function; pinout and package match to the DIP-8 NJM4558D unconfirmed.
silicon_changes.verification: NJM4558C specs from the ver.06 datasheet copy; not independently checked.

claims_confirmed: Earlier revisions G (Oct 2014), F (Sep 2010), E (Feb 2006) and D (Sep 2004) exist: https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/rc4558.pdf
Rev. D copy on the Octopart CDN: https://datasheets.b-cdn.net/files/RC4558P-Texas-Instruments-datasheet-66748.pdf

refuted_claims: SLOS073G is current: refuted; SLOS073H (Oct 2024) is current (https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/slos073h/slos073h.pdf).
Glossy vs matte JRC4558D shows 'almost no difference': partly refuted. Harmonics match, but glossy (Saga) parts are clearly quieter (https://www.jazzcaster.com/diypedal/diypedal-ts-4558d-test-2/).
SLOS073 revisions A–E not located: D (Sep 2004) and E (Feb 2006) now identified; a Rev. D copy survives on the Octopart CDN.
ST MC4558 datasheet unseen and URL inferred: the st.com URL exists (April 2012).
